members.name: Victors
hardFails: single-member card with a plural name
single-member card with a plural name
plural name on a single member (worth 1)
members.why: Rewards contest winners with more of the color they won.

members.name: Hawker
hardFails: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn
turn flow: rivals choose whether to recruit during your turn
members.why: Each rival decides in turn whether to buy during your turn, with many moving parts.

members.name: Volunteer
members.why: Blank cheap body for the red count; nothing happens when you play it.

members.name: Toastmaster
members.why: +1 follower per silver space; forgettable.

members.name: Extra Hand
members.why: One extra minion for 9 is a poor deal and the same in any cult.

members.name: Regular
members.why: +1 blue per follower buy is forgettable.

members.name: Critic
members.why: +1 follower when a rival buys blue is too small to notice.

members.name: Timekeeper
members.why: Per-purple-member scoring copies Snobs and Old Money and has nothing to do with Purple's timing.

members.name: Old Money
members.why: Per-white-member scoring copies Snobs and Timekeeper and works against White's own idea.

members.name: Patriarch
members.why: Plain wide-cult scorer with halving math; fine, not exciting.

members.name: Dyer
members.why: Same as Tourist but pays yellow; it repeats its siblings.

members.name: Snobs
members.why: Per-color-member scoring; the same shape as Timekeeper and Old Money.

members.name: Grifter
members.why: The steal grows with your cult size, so it rewards whoever is already ahead.

members.name: Heiresses
members.why: A once-per-game white bump; forgettable.

members.name: Cashier
members.why: Cash In on a member; already doable with the space.

members.name: Cheerleaders
members.why: Pays only the player already winning contests.

members.name: Line Cutters
members.why: Worth 3 for 2 and it turns off the fewest-followers-first catch-up; a must-buy for the leader.

members.name: Deprogrammers
members.why: Worth 4 for 3 resources is close to a must-buy, and the ability is a small sting on top.

members.name: Night Watch
members.why: Watching for rivals taking the token is niche, and 'per minion on it' needs a careful read.

members.name: Kidnapper
members.why: Takes the widest rival's member every round; losing members before round III feels bad.

members.name: Seamstress
members.why: 'Double your full sets' doesn't say what you gain.
members.play: no +1.17 vs Harmonist; pass +0.58 vs Harmonist

members.name: Caravan
members.why: Third copy of the per-color drip; bigger, rewards the wide leader.

members.name: Con Men
members.why: A big steal on a colorless card does Magenta's job.

members.name: Recruiter
members.why: Red income from recruiting stacks with free recruits; fine but small.

members.name: Picket Line
members.why: Taxes rivals on purple spaces; 4 cost worth 3 is cheap, effect small, same shape as High Society.

members.name: Hostesses
members.why: Steady small gifts and followers; wordy for a drip.

members.name: Caterer
members.why: Pays on any gift; unclear whether rivals' gifts count, otherwise a tidy silver link.

members.name: Smooth Talkers
members.why: Silver as any color is powerful but is the old Gold idea, not giving.

members.name: High Society
members.why: Passive follower when rivals take silver spaces; quiet.

members.name: Duty Collector
members.why: Taxes rivals' recruits in your colors; passive, no choices.

members.name: Meddler
members.why: Breaks rivals' full sets; a mild sting with fiddly choices.

members.name: Jack-of-All-Trades
members.why: A clean full-set helper that matters only to the Yellow contest.

members.name: Cutpurse
members.why: Small steal from the richest each round; checks hoards.

members.name: Misers
members.why: Saving white for the end versus spending it is a real hold-or-spend call.

members.name: Money Changers
members.why: White from everyone's follower buys; passive.

members.name: Roadie
members.why: Copy income that grows with green members; modest.

members.name: Stunt Double
members.why: Copying the action you just took when it joins is clear but one-off and small.

members.name: Agents
members.why: Shield against copying; a counter.

members.name: Mob
members.why: Pays the leader of red's contest again each round; rich-get-richer.

members.name: Charity Ball
members.why: Gift and follower whenever a rival recruits; fires often, never a decision.

members.name: Extortionist
members.why: A bigger Cutpurse; it repeats its sibling.

members.name: Barker
members.why: An extra follower buy on every member buy is strong, but the word 'recruit followers' takes a read.

members.name: Impersonator
members.why: Borrows a rival's ability; you must mark which one.

members.name: Proselytizers
members.why: A simple follower per recruit that grows with Red's free recruits; solid but quiet.

members.name: Early Birds
members.why: Cheap answer to Hold Up and Bouncers; a counter card, quiet when nobody skips.

members.name: Debt Collectors
members.why: Taking silver once runs against the color's giving.

members.name: Window Shopper
members.why: Digging the shop for resources each round fits Blue but takes two steps to read.

members.name: Trendsetters
members.why: Cheap and worth 3, but the bury repeats Window Dressers.

members.name: Bodyguards
members.why: Clean answer to all theft.

members.name: Fence
members.why: Pays you when robbed; a soft counter to magenta.

members.name: Brokers
members.why: Cheap, worth 3, and adds to every White space that pays followers.

members.name: Impressionist
members.why: A small passive on every copy at the table; quiet.

members.name: Old Maid
members.why: A curse to hand rivals via Red, Silver or Magenta; purpose not obvious alone.

members.name: Dabblers
members.why: Counting as 2 members of any color helps the member-count contests; 'wild' needs explaining.

members.name: Night Owls
members.why: A free minion every later round is strong and clear but expensive and autopilot.

members.name: Hot Streak
members.why: A big payout for chained turns, but counting 'turns in a row just before this one' is fiddly.

members.name: Gardeners
members.why: Fills color gaps each round; 'have none of' could mean members or resources.

members.name: Tourist
members.why: Followers for color variety each round; the same shape as Dyer and Caravan.

members.name: Doormen
members.why: Swap a rival's member for a shop one; strong, wording is dense.

members.name: Double Agent
members.why: A swap that plants itself in a rival's cult; reads more like Red, and the rival gets an empty card.

members.name: Raiders
members.why: A follower steal is Magenta's job.

members.name: Wallflower
members.why: Doubles every copy; a big engine for the green leader.

members.name: Alchemists
members.why: Cheap and worth 3, and it removes color limits for recruiting; overlaps Smooth Talkers.

members.name: Gossip
members.why: Feeds off every skip at the table, a passive trigger on something that happens often.

members.name: Closer
members.why: Rewards going last, which purple's contest and token already chase.

members.name: Creditor
members.why: A forced followers-for-silver trade aimed at the leader; a fair but mild sting.

members.name: Patroness
members.why: Pays off every bury at the table, a passive trigger on Blue's main action.

members.name: Window Dressers
members.why: Cheap, worth 3, with a shop refresh; combos with Patroness.

members.name: Shoplifter
members.why: Steal on every recruit; grows with recruiting.

members.name: Doppelganger
members.why: Copying your best member is strong; the table has to remember which member it copied.

members.name: Mentor & Protégés
members.why: Two members for one buy, counts 3; simple and strong for red's contest.

members.name: Panel
members.why: A free Promote or Demote on recruit; aiming it is a real choice, wording needs the space text.

members.name: Loyalists
members.why: A clean block against Red's swaps; it's unclear whether steals like Poach count as swaps.

members.name: Shopaholics
members.why: Two buys every turn is a huge engine in four words, but at 9 it's hard to Promote or Demote away.

members.name: Accomplice
members.why: A cheap way into Magenta: steal 3 when you recruit it.

members.name: Magpie
members.why: Turning everything into white sets up Cash In and Misers; it's a timing call.

members.name: Tribute Band
members.why: Do a whole rival's round once; huge, 14 cost, timing unclear.

members.name: Encore
members.why: Doubles your next On Recruit; timing decision.
members.play: bot bug -0.18 vs Chronicler; no -0.28 vs Chronicler

members.name: Anarchist
members.why: Swap any two members anywhere each round; powerful, kingmaking risk.

members.name: Sore Loser
members.why: Steals 5 from the top winner when you win nothing; catch-up with a bite.

members.name: Drifters
members.why: Cheap and flexible: counts toward any color's cards, like Mob, Snobs and Big Tent. The table needs a marker for the chosen color.

members.name: Recluse
members.why: Pays for staying small; the white idea in one line, fair catch-up.

members.name: Body Snatchers
members.why: Equal-cost swap each round; a fair sting Loyalists answers.

members.name: Courier
members.why: Rewards purple's in-a-row turns with every other color; builds toward full sets.

members.name: Debutantes
members.why: Doubling your silver once is a big, well-timed contest swing with a small gift attached.

members.name: Big Tent
members.why: Exactly one per color is a crisp build goal that shapes every recruit.

members.name: Desperado
members.why: Bigger steals for the trailing player; a true catch-up card.

members.name: Song Request
members.why: An extra copy each round of a rival's space; strong and it reads the table.

members.name: Fan Club
members.why: Copying the leader's space is catch-up with a clear target.

members.name: Party Crasher
members.why: Take a blocked space once; breaks the draft for a big turn.

members.name: Foster Parents
members.why: Rewards Promote, Demote, Poach and swaps with +2 each time; ties Red's moving members to followers in very few words.
members.play: pass +1.08 vs Greeters; pass +0.87 vs Greeters

members.name: Godparent
members.why: Give a member away for its cost; links to Foster Parents and Old Maid.

members.name: Guest of Honor
members.why: Dumping a cheap member for +4 every round is strong and aimable; it combos with cheap filler and Old Maid.

members.name: Spoilsport
members.why: Cancelling a contest you can't win is clear catch-up, and everyone can plan around it.

members.name: Bouncers
members.why: Skip two rivals on recruit; a visible jolt that costs nobody a minion.

members.name: Second-Story Man
members.why: A theft right before contests are scored can swing a contest, and everyone sees it coming.

members.name: Martyrs
members.why: Leaving pays its cost, so Farewell, Godparent and thieves all feed it; few words that play off the whole board.

spaces.name: Shake Down
hardFails: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn; victim chooses their own punishment
turn flow: the rival chooses during your turn, and chooses their own punishment
spaces.why: The victim picks their own punishment on your turn, and that feels bad.

spaces.name: Potluck
hardFails: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn
turn flow: each rival chooses a resource to give during your turn
spaces.why: Each rival picks what to hand over during your turn, and they always give their least useful resource.

spaces.name: Build Up
spaces.why: The plain green anchor.

spaces.name: Stash
spaces.why: Same text as Gather and Allowance; nothing magenta about it.

spaces.name: Allowance
spaces.why: Same text as Gather and Stash; not white's idea.

spaces.name: Gather
spaces.why: Plain red income with a small recruit bonus; it's the color's anchor space, so its quiet sting is fine.

spaces.name: Sweet Talk
spaces.why: Silver plus conversion; repeats Polish one ring later.

spaces.name: Polish
spaces.why: A plain converter that does Yellow's job; useful but flat.

spaces.name: Exchange
spaces.why: Resources into followers at 2 for 1, a small, plain conversion.

spaces.name: Demote
spaces.why: Mirror of Promote; taking a cheaper member is weaker and is mostly a way to dump a card or feed Foster Parents.

spaces.name: Right Away
spaces.why: Two turns in a row is clean; the small payout makes it mostly a way to set up Courier.

spaces.name: Harvest
spaces.why: Yellow's anchor: plain resources in colors you pick.

spaces.name: Leaders' Tax
spaces.why: Reads where rivals are; the count is easy but the choice takes a look.

spaces.name: New Blood
spaces.why: Rewards a new color recruit; clear but the bonus is modest.

spaces.name: Savings
spaces.why: Blue income plus a shop dig before you recruit; the optional step is easy to forget.

spaces.name: Estate Sale
spaces.why: Farewell for white instead; a sibling.

spaces.name: Splurge
spaces.why: Followers for an expensive recruit; round III rate unstated.

spaces.name: Tryout
spaces.why: Borrowing any shop member's On Recruit plays off the whole shop; the copying leans green.

spaces.name: Melting Pot
spaces.why: Pays for a wide cult; the wide player is usually ahead.

spaces.name: Sleep In
spaces.why: Big purple for going last is a real timing trade, but the Goes Last token takes a rules read.

spaces.name: Last Call
spaces.why: Pays for holding minions back; strong but the token interaction is fiddly.

spaces.name: Peek
spaces.why: Stacking the pile and picking from it is a strong shop play, but wordy.

spaces.name: Bury
spaces.why: Denying a shop member pays a little; the half-cost math adds words.

spaces.name: Reprise
spaces.why: Doubling your own best action is clear; it's quieter than Echo.

spaces.name: Sample
spaces.why: Borrow a rival's On Recruit; reads the table.

spaces.name: Cover
spaces.why: Copy an empty space; flexible.

spaces.name: Walk-In
spaces.why: A free member off the top of the pile is exciting, and the +1 red to each rival softens it; few words.

spaces.name: Overtime
spaces.why: An extra minion in round III is an obvious burst.

spaces.name: Toast
spaces.why: Big silver for you with a gift to everyone is the giving idea in one line.

spaces.name: Makeover
spaces.why: Rearranging every resource in round III can flip contests and complete full sets at the last moment.

spaces.name: Cash In
spaces.why: A round III cash-out that rewards having saved white; one clear line.

spaces.name: Initiation
spaces.why: A free 8-cost recruit in round III is a big burst a trailing player can grab.

spaces.name: Recruit Twice
spaces.why: Two buys in one turn is clear and strong.

spaces.name: Lie Low
spaces.why: A small steal plus a shield; a clean defensive choice.

spaces.name: Farewell
spaces.why: Casting out a member for its cost in followers combos with Martyrs; clear and punchy.

spaces.name: Greatest Hits
spaces.why: Replays your whole On Recruit set; the round III payoff.

spaces.name: Hold Up
spaces.why: Skip the next turn, even your own; a visible block with a timing call.

spaces.name: Crunch Time
spaces.why: Three turns in a row is a big swing on the snake in few words, and it's a burst anyone can use to catch up.

spaces.name: Housewarming
spaces.why: A free new-color member; widening in one move.

spaces.name: Spree
spaces.why: Three recruits in round III is a burst any trailing player can use.

spaces.name: Help Yourself
spaces.why: Scaling split steal; the color's core in one line.

spaces.name: Heist
spaces.why: Stealing followers directly is a big, aimable swing at the leader.

spaces.name: Largesse
spaces.why: A round III giveaway with a clear payoff and kingmaking tension; overlaps Party Gifts.

spaces.name: Poach
spaces.why: Take any rival member free in round III; a big, clear moment.

spaces.name: Echo
spaces.why: Copy the previous action; scales with what the table takes.

spaces.name: Promote
spaces.why: Trading up with a rival is the heart of Red; the victim gets a member back so it stings fairly, and it works as catch-up.

spaces.name: Party Gifts
spaces.why: Choosing who gets your silver gifts, with the silver contest at stake, is a real and social decision.

spaces.name: Out of Style
spaces.why: Wiping one color from the shop blocks rivals in plain sight and pays per card sent away.
